title: Point at Which the Review Ceiling Bites on an Excess Withdrawal Fee Review
content:
Where the review ceiling bites on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts follows the withdrawal history of the account: the count of withdrawals posted to it in the three calendar months ending on the review date.

Where 4 or more withdrawals posted in that window, the review ceiling binds the reviewable fee pool before the fee units are applied.

Where 2 or 3 withdrawals posted in that window, the review ceiling binds the credit after the fee units have been applied.

Where fewer than 2 withdrawals posted in that window, the fee units alone govern the credit booked.

### Why the point matters

Take a hypothetical reviewable fee pool of 90.00 USD, a unit entitlement of 36.00 USD and a review ceiling of 24.00 USD.

With 5 withdrawals in the window, the ceiling binds the pool first: the pool of 90.00 USD is held at 24.00 USD, and that is the credit booked.

With 3 withdrawals, the fee units are applied first: the lesser of the pool of 90.00 USD and the entitlement of 36.00 USD is 36.00 USD, which the ceiling then holds at 24.00 USD.

With 1 withdrawal, the fee units alone govern: the credit booked is the lesser of 90.00 USD and 36.00 USD, that is 36.00 USD, and the ceiling does not bind at all.

### Boundary of the counts

A count of exactly 4 withdrawals falls in the first band, a count of exactly 2 in the second, and a count of 1 or 0 in the third.
